what_it_does: Running large AI language models on FPGAs (reprogrammable chips, as opposed to fixed-function chips like GPUs) is attractive for edge deployments, but these models are huge and slow unless their numbers are compressed. One common compression trick is to round the model's internal weights to fewer decimal places (called quantization), which lets you pack more numbers into the same memory and compute results faster. A known pitfall is that a small fraction of weights have unusually large values (called outliers) that resist rounding well and degrade accuracy. DuoQ removes those outliers through a learned mathematical transformation during training, then applies aggressive 4-bit compression (using only 16 possible values per number rather than billions) uniformly across all weights. The chip design is also tuned to match the specific math units (called DSPs — digital signal processing blocks) built into FPGAs, squeezing out extra efficiency.
